title: Codility Product Update: November 2026 | Codility Lab

How do you judge how well a candidate uses AI?
When a candidate builds with an AI assistant, the record of how they did it is the transcript: every prompt, every answer, every change. It holds everything, and few reviewers read it end to end for every candidate. AI Usage Insights already showed how much a candidate used AI. It could not show how well.
Task reports in Screen, Interview and Skills Intelligence now carry an AI skills section. It covers 5 AI skills. Each skill opens evidence cards with the candidate’s own words and one sentence on why they show that skill. Every quote must match the transcript word for word, so a reviewer can check any card in seconds and turn it into a follow-up question for the interview.
The evidence informs your review and never changes the score. Codility gives your hiring team the evidence, and your team makes the final decision.
Read why
detecting AI use is the wrong hiring question
Can candidates use Codex in a Codility assessment?
Yes. Since October 19, 2026, OpenAI’s Codex CLI runs next to Claude Code in the VS Code terminal, in Screen, Interview and Skills Intelligence. Candidates pick the agent they already use at work.
In Interview, you and the candidate share the same live terminal, so you see each prompt and answer as it happens. The hidden instructions you give the coding agent in Interview now work with Codex too, so you can ask either agent to slip in a bug and see who reviews the code. Codex conversations are saved to the report, and AI Usage Insights show Codex and Claude Code separately. AI skills evidence works with both.

Log in to Codility
How do you see how a candidate designs a system?
System design usually gets judged at a whiteboard, from what a candidate says they would build. In InfraLab and TicketDrop, two new tasks in the Advanced library, the candidate builds the system on a board. A simulator replays traffic against it, and the load lab shows the symptoms, so you see how the candidate finds the cause and fixes it.
TicketDrop suits backend engineers who own a whole system. InfraLab suits DevOps, cloud and site reliability engineers. Both are scored automatically, with no code to write.

What else changes for your hiring team?
Different tasks for each candidate, on every account
In a large hiring round, a task every candidate sees is a task that gets shared. The Task Randomizer is now on for every account. Each task in an assessment can become a pool of comparable tasks, so the next candidate gets a different one.
The same approved tasks for every interviewer
When each interviewer picks their own task, candidates in the same round get different interviews, and comparing them gets harder. With task collections, a team agrees on the tasks once and shares them across the account. Interviewers open them straight from the task selector.
